After applying the algorithm to half a million genomes in the U.K. Biobank cohort detailing the training, the results showed unprecedented accuracy.

The rapid emergence of the ETF industry, marked by its AuM growth from $1 trillion to $10 trillion this past decade, was driven by passive indexed funds which thrived in a low-rates, low-volatility environment. These funds offered low cost, low differentiation solutions to retail investors.  
As institutional investors overtake retail investors in ETF adoption, the landscape of the industry is set for a paradigm shift. The limitations of indexes are becoming increasingly apparent in a macro environment characterized by higher rates and higher volatility, which could stick around in the decade to come. The fundamental analysis and risk management that had been left behind by index funds are suddenly relevant again. Investors are consequently exploring alternative vehicles for their public equity exposures, namely active ETFs. 
Tema is one of the first independent thematic active ETF asset managers, but unlike competitors, is concentrating on underpenetrated, generational thematic trends that were previously inaccessible to investors. These themes include reshoring, oncology, luxury goods, cardiology and metabolics (Obesity and diabetes), and monopolies and oligopolies. 
The vulnerabilities of passive ETFs are becoming more apparent in the current environment 
Limited by the rigid nature of their underlying indices, passive funds lack the ability to dynamically respond and adapt to increasingly rapid and sharp changes in environment. These limitations undermine risk management efficacy and can ultimately compound risks for their investors. 
An example is the special premature rebalance the Nasdaq 100 index had to undergo this past summer. The disparity in performance within the index had over-concentrated its value, with the “Magnificent seven”, Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Apple (NASDAQ: APPL), Meta (NASDAQ: META), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), and Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA), reaching 55% of the index’s total value. Ready for a new week of sound money advocacy? Let’s dive in:


Argentina Votes to #EndTheFed:


Argentina is a country I love. I’ve visited multiple times and have wonderful friends who live there. It’s also been the multi-decade poster child for bad fiscal management. The government overspends in a way that would make the US Congress blush, and regularly defaults on its debt. The inflation rate has risen from 100% when I visited last winter to over 140% now. In response, they just elected Javier Milei, a political outsider, libertarian, and sound money advocate. He wants to reduce the size of the government, slash spending, embrace Bitcoin, disband the central bank (#EndTheFed), and reduce inflation by switching to a dollar standard. Many are calling him the first anarcho capitalist President in the world.

Here's Milei looking much less manic than usual.
DKI Takeaway:  DKI is thrilled to see Argentina embrace freedom and sound money. (Click the link to see a series of stories about how hard life is in Argentina with massive inflation.) If Milei succeeds, it will be a painful transition, but the country will be much better off long-term. I hope I’m wrong about this, but Milei is facing a steep hurdle to succeed. As a political outsider, he doesn’t have the loyalty of the legislature. He’ll also be fought by the labor unions and the government bureaucracy that will be loath to give up their cushy guaranteed jobs. We can expect these groups to try to sabotage Milei’s plans. On behalf of DKI and freedom-lovers everywhere, we wish Argentina and its people nothing but success and a bright future.

As we have been sharing with you, several market mechanics have been driving the stock market up. One of those market mechanics is 0DTE options. Everyday traders have been aggressively buying 0DTE calls. Everyday when the market started going up, market makers were forced to buy stocks to hedge the calls they had sold.
During the rally, market makers were more than happy to sell puts to investors as everyday puts expired worthless, resulting in market makers making huge profits. As the rally continued, market makers stopped hedging the puts they were selling. After all, there was no point in hedging because the stock market went up everyday.

The weak Treasury auction caused the stock market to turn down. Market makers were caught flat footed as they had sold lots of puts without hedging. As the market went down, market makers were forced to sell stocks to hedge the puts they had sold.
The result of the surprise encountered by market makers was they were forced to sell stocks to hedge, causing the biggest sell-off since September.
The sell-off came just before the traditional Santa Claus rally.
Traditionally, the Santa Claus rally starts tomorrow.

SOXX has a lower expense ratio (0.34% vs 0.38%) and higher dividend yield (0.5% vs 0.1%), but IYW offers reduced volatility and exposure to non-semiconductor AI players like Alphabet.

title: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg Just Delivered Great News for Nvidia and Micron Investors
summary: Meta raised its capital expenditure forecast to $125-145 billion (from $115-135 billion), citing higher component costs, particularly memory pricing. This signals continued strong AI spending across hyperscalers, with Google Cloud growing 63%, Azure up 39%, and AWS at 28%. Nvidia and Micron are positioned to benefit from increased capex and higher chip prices, which improve margins. The commentary suggests the AI investment boom is still in early stages with several more years of growth expected.

title: Meet the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Infrastructure Stock That Has Crushed Nvidia and Broadcom With a 270% Jump. It Can Still Fly Higher.
summary: Vertiv, an AI data center infrastructure company specializing in power management and cooling solutions, has surged 270% over the past year, significantly outperforming Nvidia (95%) and Broadcom (117%). The company raised its 2026 guidance with 51% earnings growth expected, driven by strong Q1 results showing 30% revenue growth and 83% earnings growth. Analysts suggest the stock could climb another 44% based on projected 2028 earnings, as the data center cooling market is expected to grow 5x by 2033.

title: Stock Market Today: Dow Jones Roars As Industrials Rescue Wall Street From Meta-Led Tech Slide
summary: The Dow Jones surged 1.5% driven by industrial and healthcare stocks, while mega-cap tech faced pressure from concerns over AI capital spending. Meta and Microsoft declined on capex worries, but Alphabet gained on enterprise AI wins. Industrials like Caterpillar, Quanta Services, and Carrier rallied on data-center infrastructure demand. The S&P 500 gained 0.5% while the Nasdaq 100 remained flat.

title: S&P 500 Edges Higher Amid Mixed Mega-Cap Earnings; Dow Leads Market Indexes Overall
summary: U.S. stock indexes rose on April 30, 2026, with the Dow leading gains driven by Caterpillar's 10% surge on strong earnings. Mega-cap tech earnings were mixed: Alphabet soared 9.6% on robust Google Cloud revenue growth, while Meta and Microsoft fell on concerns about massive AI infrastructure spending. Nvidia declined 4.3% amid competition concerns. The market showed investors are now scrutinizing which companies convert AI hype into actual revenue.

title: 3 Stocks I'd Rather Own Than Apple With a CEO Shakeup
summary: With Tim Cook stepping down as Apple CEO in September 2026 and John Ternus taking over, the article argues that leadership transitions create uncertainty. Apple trades at a premium valuation (34x earnings) without strong growth prospects and lacks a clear AI strategy. The author recommends Nvidia, Microsoft, and Alphabet as better investment alternatives due to their strong AI exposure, cloud computing growth, and more attractive valuations.

title: Prediction: These Will Be the Next $5 Trillion Companies
summary: The article predicts that Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon will become $5 trillion companies, following Nvidia's achievement. Their cloud computing businesses, powered by AI demand, are positioned to drive massive growth. Alphabet needs less than 20% growth to reach the target, while Microsoft could benefit from valuation expansion, and Amazon's highly profitable AWS segment generates most operating income.

title: Microsoft Earnings Look Strong, But Investors Focus on Risks
summary: Microsoft delivered strong Q3 2026 earnings with 40% Azure growth and $37 billion in AI revenue, but shares fell 5% post-earnings due to investor concerns over $190 billion annual capex spending and OpenAI relationship risks. Despite solid fundamentals and a 37% upside from consensus price targets, market sentiment remains cautious about potential AI bubble and OpenAI revenue sustainability.

title: Nvidia vs. Intel: Diverging Paths in Quarterly Revenue
summary: Nvidia demonstrates substantially stronger revenue performance than Intel, posting eight consecutive quarters of rising revenue with a 73% year-over-year increase in Q4 2024, while Intel's revenue has remained largely flat. Despite Intel's recent 7% year-over-year growth in Q1 2025—its highest in eight quarters—Nvidia's trailing-12-month revenue of $188 billion dwarfs Intel's $53 billion. Both companies are benefiting from AI demand, but Nvidia's GPU dominance and higher profit margins position it to continue widening its financial gap.

title: Bulldozer Maker Caterpillar Delivers Twice Nvidia's Returns — What's Behind The Move?
summary: Caterpillar has outperformed Nvidia significantly, returning 185% over the past year compared to Nvidia's 85%. The catalyst is Caterpillar's emergence as an AI infrastructure play, driven by hyperscalers building on-site gas-fired power plants to bypass grid interconnect delays. Q1 2026 results showed a record $63 billion backlog and 41% surge in power generation revenue. The company plans to expand large reciprocating engine capacity to nearly three times 2024 levels, with heavy investments through 2029. Most analysts maintain Buy ratings with price targets ranging from $430 to $960, though debate centers on valuation multiples rather than business fundamentals.

title: Why Is Meta Stock Crashing, and is it a Generational Buying Opportunity?
summary: Meta Platforms' stock dropped 8.5% following Q1 2026 earnings results, with the decline attributed to higher artificial intelligence capital expenditure outlook despite strong quarterly performance. The sharp sell-off raises questions about whether this represents a buying opportunity for long-term investors.
